children: Ghana's government said on Thursday it bought back 12.6 billion Ghana cedis ($1.06 billion) of bonds maturing in February 2027 in the first round of a voluntary buyback, using money from its Cedi Sinking Fund.
The bonds tendered represent 44.1% of the outstanding stock, the Ministry of Finance statement said
The statement said participating bondholders were paid in full and in cash
Total payments came to GH¢12.89 billion ($1.09 billion), including GH¢289 million in accrued interest
The government said the bonds were bought at an auction and were issued under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme
The government said it would reopen the offer in two weeks, so holders of the remaining February 2027 bonds can tender them in a second round

Ghana defaulted in December 2022 after an economic crisis triggered by rising global interest rates and soaring inflation in the wake of the pandemic, as well as government overspending and economic mismanagement
